title: Bottom-cohomology comparison normalized by the actual right-derived unit
statement: Let C and D be abelian categories with derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], and suppose C has enough injectives and K-injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let S:C→D be additive and left exact, and n an integer. There exists a natural isomorphism delta:H^n(RS(tau_GE_n(-)))→S(H^n(-)), where tau_GE is the standard lower truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For every cochain complex K, left homology data T for K and U for S(K) in degree n, and map k:S(T.K)→U.K satisfying S(T.i)=k composed with U.i, the composite k, U.pi, inverse U.homologyIso, inverse Q/homology comparison, homology of the actual right-derived unit at K, homology of RS applied to the lower-truncation projection QK→tau_GE_n(QK), and delta at QK equals S applied to T.pi, inverse T.homologyIso and inverse Q/homology comparison. No affine geometry, quasi-coherence, exact module-valued functor F, or invertibility of the derived lower-truncation projection is assumed or concluded.

source.place: 05TC (2), upper truncation of the lower-truncated object; the degree-zero left-exact comparison and its unit, as used in 08D4 with bound one and in the 0AVW cohomology display.

proof.text: Construct the bottom comparison by the double-truncation argument of new-qcoh-sections-left-exact-bottom. Lift lower truncation at n to the bounded-below category; upper truncate at n and use 05TC (2) to identify degree-n derived homology. Double truncation is the degree-n cohomology object in degree n. Shift to degree zero and use the single-object comparison followed by rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf, which is the inverse of the actual degree-zero unit for a left exact functor. Transport through bounded-below/unbounded compatibility. This specifies a natural comparison; an arbitrary isomorphism witness is not sufficient.

Represent the lower truncation projection by the smart truncation of a complex K. Naturality of the right-derived unit reduces the displayed equation to the bottom-degree calculation on that truncated complex. A cycle of K maps to its class in the degree-n kernel of the smart truncation. The double-truncation identification sends it to the same class in H^n(K), and the degree-zero derived unit sends it to that class in an injective resolution. The bottom comparison inverts that unit. Thus the composite equals S applied to the cycle quotient. Left exactness preserves the cycle kernel. The equality S(T.i)=k followed by U.i identifies the cycle maps by monicity of U.i; kernel uniqueness and the homology-data cokernel quotient give the formula for any T and U. The construction is natural in complex maps and descends to the derived category; Plus compatibility preserves the unit, giving exactly the displayed unbounded-unit formula. This argument does not assert that R(S) inverts the lower-truncation projection.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_rightDerivedFunctor_truncated_bottom_unit
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C]
    [EnoughInjectives C] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions C]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wC} C]
    {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} D]
    (S : C ⥤ D) [S.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits S] (n : ℤ) :
    ∃ δ : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE n ⋙ S.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor D n ≅
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor C n ⋙ S,
      ∀ (K : CochainComplex C ℤ)
        (T : (K.sc n).LeftHomologyData)
        (U : (((S.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K).sc n).LeftHomologyData)
        (k : S.obj T.K ⟶ U.K),
        S.map T.i = k ≫ U.i →
        k ≫ U.π ≫ U.homologyIso.inv ≫
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors D n).app
            ((S.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)).inv ≫
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor D n).map
            (S.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient C (.up ℤ)).obj K)) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor D n).map
            (S.rightDerivedFunctor.map
              ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ n).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))) ≫
          δ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) =
        S.map (T.π ≫ T.homologyIso.inv ≫
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors C n).app K).inv)
